newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-LAWLESS PUTS NATAL ON TOP.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LAWLESS PUTS NATAL ON TOP.

text.p: The Natal Sharks underlined their Super 12 title credentials with a 33-15 win over the Waikato Chiefs in Auckland which put them top of the table for at least 24 hours on Friday.
Full-back Gavin Lawless, who scored a record 50 points against Otago last month, contributed another 18 points with the boot and converted all three of his side's tries.
Natal pushed the offside laws to the limit in their attempts to put pressure on the Waikato defence and their pack had the edge up front from an early stage.

Even so, they led only 6-3 after 34 minutes when the game took a decisive turn. Waikato prop Richard Loe was yellow-carded for handling the ball on the ground near the line and hooker Paul Mitchell was sin-binned. From the ensuing penalty close to the line prop Adrian Garvey went over for a converted try.
Two minutes into the second half the Chiefs were penalised again to allow Lawless a third successful penalty and his fourth kick 15 minutes into the second half left the Chiefs hanging on.
Their fears were realised midway through the half when Springbok lock Mark Andrews took a two-handed ball on the Waikato 22 and Natal worked winger Cabous Van Der Westhuizen over for a try.
The Chiefs' efforts were rewarded four minutes from the end when Glenn Taylor barged over for a converted try, only for Garvey's second try to inflict further punishment.

Natal's lead in the standings could be short-lived depending on the outcome of Saturday's encounter between Auckland and ACT and the South African showdown between Gauteng Lions (formerly Transvaal) and Northern Transvaal.

Natal Sharks - Gavin Lawless; Joost Joubert, Jeremy Thomson, Jeff Appleford, Cabous van der Westhuizen; Henry Honiball, Kevin Putt; Gary Teichmann (captain), Wayne Fyvie, John Slade, Mark Andrews, Wickus van Heerden, Adrian Garvey, John Allan, Rob Kempson.

Waikato Chiefs - Bruce Reihana; Eric Rush, Frank Bunce, Walter Little, Glen Osborne; Blair Feeney, Rhys Duggan; Deon Muir, Dean Anglesey, Ian Jones (captain), Glenn Taylor, Errol Brain, Richard Loe, Paul Mitchell, Michael Collins.
